text:
maya: Heads-up — nightly eval showed a sudden spike in failures for redwood-3b-quantized-v2 on the multilingual promptset (esp. ja/ko).  failure rate jumped from ~2% to 18% across the suite.

sam: ugh, saw that too. any noisy infra alerts?

maya: no infra CPU/GPU alarms. I dug into a few failing examples and the model outputs look like binary garbage or truncated text. sample id 20260320-4873 has output: 
```
��

�
```
which is... not right.

lina: did the tokenizer change? or is this an encoding/decoding issue when reading prompts?

alex: I pulled the prompt bundle from S3 and tried a quick run locally — got the same garbage. S3 GET returned header ContentEncoding: gzip but body was not gzipped. boto3 is returning the header as-is.

sam: interesting — so harness is doing `open_stream(...).read()` and then `gzip.decompress(...)` because it trusts the header. if body isn't compressed, decompress throws or returns garbage depending on input.

maya: logs from nightly-runner show this stack repeatedly: 
```
File "eval_harness/io.py", line 212, in load_prompt_bundle
  data = gzip.decompress(raw)
OSError: Not a gzipped file (b'\x1f\x8b')
```
(weirdly sometimes it raises, sometimes downstream code treats bytes as text and we get mojibake).

nate: deploy-bot rolled the prompt-bundler lambda yesterday at 02:12 UTC (release 2026.3.19-b). deploy-bot: can you paste the deploy?

deploy-bot: release pushed: prompt-bundler v2.4.0 by lina at 2026-03-19T02:12:07Z. CI: passed.

lina: that release changed how we proxy S3 assets through the edge — we started preserving ContentEncoding from origin instead of normalizing. looks like some older bundles were uploaded without gzip but still had the header set incorrectly. the normalizer previously fixed this.

alex: quick repro snippet I used: 
```
import requests
r = requests.get('https://assets.redwood.ai/prompt-bundles/multilingual-20260319.tar')
print(r.headers.get('Content-Encoding'))
print(r.content[:64])
```
header = 'gzip', but content begins with `PK\x03\x04` (tar gz vs zip confusion) — some bundles are zipped, some gzipped, header inconsistent.

sam: so harness trusts header -> tries gzip.decompress -> sometimes fails or produces garbage -> scoring sees mismatch and counts as failure. makes sense.

nate: mitigation options: 1) revert prompt-bundler normalization change, 2) make eval harness robust: detect compression by magic bytes instead of header, 3) sanitize existing S3 objects (bulk fix). I'd push quick guard in harness first so nightly doesn't keep flapping.

maya: agree. can we add a small function `detect_and_decompress(raw_bytes)` and fall back to plain text if detect fails? keep it defensive.

lina: I'll revert the edge change for now and kick off a background job to validate existing bundles.

alex: I'll open a PR with the harness guard and a small unit test covering zipped, gzipped, and uncompressed bundles. patch includes: 
```
MAGIC_GZIP = b'\x1f\x8b'
MAGIC_ZIP = b'PK\x03\x04'

def detect_and_decompress(raw):
  if raw.startswith(MAGIC_GZIP):
    return gzip.decompress(raw)
  if raw.startswith(MAGIC_ZIP):
    return zlib.decompress(raw)  # or use zipfile
  try:
    return raw.decode('utf-8')
  except UnicodeDecodeError:
    raise ValueError('unknown bundle encoding')
```

nate: tiny nit: for zip use `zipfile` to extract, not zlib. also log a metric for `bundle_encoding:unknown` so we can alert if we see weird formats.

maya: thanks — can we also re-run the failing subset before next scheduled nightly? if harness guard + revert edge go in, we can verify.

lina: revert done (edge rolled back to normalize header) and started validation job (s3 list + head checks).

alex: PR opened: #8421 — added robust loader + tests + metric emitted. running CI now.

eval-ci: rerun requested: nightly-subset/ja-ko (50 prompt samples) queued.

sam: will monitor. if we still see flakiness after this, we should consider moving bundles to immutable storage and adding upload-time validation.

maya: awesome teamwork. follow-up actions: lina will clean S3 mismatched objects, alex will land harness guard, nate will add metric alert, sam will monitor nightly subset results.

lina: FYI I'll post a short doc in #eng-ml about the bundle format and upload checklist so other teams don't accidentally upload bad headers. :memo:

maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
